name: ARTEMIS P1 and P2
short_status: Operating: 15 years in lunar orbit, with fresh magnetometer files from both probes on Berkeley's public data server through October 24, 2026 (as of October 26, 2026).
tagline: NASA · United States · Orbiter · 2011 · The robotic return Operating
stats: recycled heliophysics probes in lunar orbit
in lunar orbit, as of October 2026
spacecraft ever to orbit an Earth-Moon Lagrange point
delta-V left on P1 for the entire Moon transfer, forcing the slow low-energy route

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 17 February 2007, at 6:01 p.m. EST on a Delta II from Cape Canaveral pad 17-B; all five THEMIS probes rode a single rocket

facts.label: Two acronyms
facts.value: THEMIS is Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms; the lunar extension is ARTEMIS, Acceleration, Reconnection, Turbulence and Electrodynamics of the Moon's Interaction with the Sun

facts.label: Which probes
facts.value: THEMIS B became ARTEMIS P1 and THEMIS C became ARTEMIS P2 under the lunar extension NASA approved, announced 19 May 2008; THEMIS A, D and E stayed in Earth orbit

facts.label: Why they left Earth orbit
facts.value: The two outermost probes were drifting into ever longer eclipse seasons that would have frozen the solar-powered spacecraft; orbit-raising maneuvers to escape began 20 July 2009

facts.label: Fuel budget
facts.value: At the start of the lunar transfer P1 had 14.5 kg of hydrazine (307 m/s of delta-V) and P2 had 21.1 kg (450 m/s), so navigators flew a low-energy route lasting well over a year, with lunar and solar gravity doing most of the work

facts.label: Lagrange point first
facts.value: P1 is the first spacecraft ever to navigate to and hold orbit around the Earth-Moon L1 and L2 Lagrange points

facts.label: Arrival milestones
facts.value: P1 reached the L2 Lagrange point on 25 August 2010, and P2 reached L1 on 22 October 2010; P1 entered lunar orbit 27 June 2011, and P2 followed 17 July 2011

facts.label: Lunar orbits
facts.value: Stable, equatorial, high-eccentricity orbits of roughly 100 by 19,000 kilometers altitude with periods near 26 hours, one probe prograde and one retrograde so their apsides sweep the full circle of local times

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: Five per probe: an Electric Field Instrument, Fluxgate Magnetometer, Search Coil Magnetometer, Electrostatic Analyzer and Solid State Telescope, giving two-point plasma and field measurements around the Moon

facts.label: 2023 senior review
facts.value: The review found every minor sensor anomaly recovered or worked around, with sensors returning to full science capability on all probes; the panel called ARTEMIS support for the crewed Artemis program and Lunar Gateway compelling, noting continuation costs far less than launching replacement spacecraft to the Moon

facts.label: FY2026 closeout scare
facts.value: NASA's May 2025 budget request ordered THEMIS, and with it ARTEMIS, to implement mission closeout

facts.label: Congress said no
facts.value: The enacted FY2026 appropriations rejected the proposed science cuts and funded NASA heliophysics at $874.8 million, with NASA science at $7.25 billion

facts.label: Still returning data
facts.value: Berkeley's public data server holds P1 and P2 fluxgate magnetometer files through 24 October 2026, both posted on 26 October 2026 (as of 26 October 2026)

timeline: Five THEMIS probes launch on a single Delta II from Cape Canaveral pad 17-B
Feb 2008
The five-probe constellation catches magnetic reconnection triggering an auroral substorm, the parent mission's headline result
Berkeley announces NASA's approval: THEMIS B and C will go to the Moon under the new name ARTEMIS
Orbit-raising maneuvers begin, pulling the two probes out of Earth orbits whose deepening eclipses would have frozen them
P1 becomes the first spacecraft ever to orbit an Earth-Moon Lagrange point, arriving at L2
P2 arrives at the L1 Lagrange point on the Earth-facing side of the Moon
P1 enters lunar orbit after a two-year transfer flown mostly on gravity assists
P2 enters lunar orbit; the pair settle into opposing elliptical orbits for two-point measurements
Coordinated observations support NASA's LADEE exosphere mission from lunar orbit
May 2019
NASA names its crewed lunar program Artemis, eleven years after these probes took the name
Heliophysics senior review endorses continued operations, with sensors back at full science capability on all probes after minor recovered anomalies
May 2025
The FY2026 budget request orders THEMIS mission closeout
The FY2026 appropriations minibus H.R. 6938 is signed into law, sealing Congress's rejection of the science cuts
The latest magnetometer files from both probes on Berkeley's public server are for this date (as of October 26, 2026); 15 years in lunar orbit and both probes still working
